item.title: How to Create n8n Agent Skills: Write SKILL.md Files That Teach Coding Agents to Build Better Workflows
item.description:
Introduction

Coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode can generate n8n workflows from a plain-English description, but unguided output is unreliable. Agents invent node parameters that do not exist, guess typeVersion numbers, and paste API keys straight into workflow JSON. An Agent Skill, a SKILL.md markdown file plus optional references and scripts, encodes your team’s n8n conventions so the agent generates workflows that actually import. This tutorial shows how to author one, following n8n’s own skill authoring guide that landed in the n8n repository in mid-September 2026.

item.title: How to Add an MCP Server to Cursor
item.description:
Introduction

Adding an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to Cursor gives the AI agent access to tools outside your codebase, a filesystem reader, a database, a web fetcher, your GitHub issues. This guide walks you through the full process using a real example server, verified against the official Cursor docs, and ends with a test you can run in Agent chat to prove it works.

Quick answer

To add an MCP server to Cursor, create a .cursor/mcp.json file in your project (or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects) with a top-level {"mcpServers": {...}} object describing each server, then restart Cursor and confirm the green status dot on Cursor Settings → MCP.
